elements.label: Your first week working for Nanami Kento had been quieter than you expected. Not easier—just quieter., There was something about the man that made people lower their voices whenever he walked past. Perhaps it was his position as the company's CFO, or the reputation he'd built over the years. Everyone on the executive floor seemed to know him, yet very few seemed to actually know him., You had been warned before accepting the position., Nanami is particular. He likes things done properly. Don't be late. And whatever you do, don't waste his time., So you learned quickly., You learned how he preferred his documents arranged, which meetings he considered important, which calls could wait, and which reports needed to be on his desk before he even asked for them. You also learned that he rarely worked without a cup of coffee beside him., It was Friday morning when you arrived at his office a few minutes earlier than usual. The executive floor was still relatively quiet, sunlight spilling through the enormous windows and turning the glass walls pale gold., You knocked softly., "Come in.", Nanami was already working., He sat behind his desk with his sleeves neatly buttoned, glasses resting low against his nose as he read through a report. His attention didn't immediately leave the page when you entered., You placed the documents on his desk in the order you'd prepared them., His eyes moved through the first few pages before he gave a small nod., "Good.", That single word had somehow become one of the few forms of praise you'd learned to recognize from him., You turned toward your desk outside his office, but before you could leave, his voice stopped you., "Your schedule.", You looked back., He gestured toward the chair across from him. You sat and began going through the day's appointments while he listened quietly, occasionally making a note or checking the time on his watch., There was something strangely reassuring about the routine., Despite his intimidating reputation, Nanami had never been unfair to you. When you made a mistake, he corrected it without humiliating you. When you finished something well, he acknowledged it without unnecessary praise. He simply expected you to learn and trusted you to do better the next time., By lunchtime, you'd been working for nearly four hours without noticing., A cup of coffee suddenly appeared beside your keyboard., You looked up., Nanami was already walking back toward his office., "You've been staring at that screen for too long," he said, not even turning around. "Take your lunch.", Your eyes dropped to the cup., It was exactly the way you usually ordered it., You hadn't told him how you liked it., At least, you didn't remember telling him., Before you could ask, the door to his office closed quietly behind him., You stared at the coffee for a moment., Then, despite yourself, you smiled., Maybe working for Nanami Kento wouldn't be as difficult as everyone had made it sound.

elements.text: By lunchtime, you'd been working for nearly four hours without noticing.
A cup of coffee suddenly appeared beside your keyboard.
Nanami was already walking back toward his office.
"You've been staring at that screen for too long," he said, not even turning around. "Take your lunch."
Your eyes dropped to the cup.
It was exactly the way you usually ordered it.
You hadn't told him how you liked it.
At least, you didn't remember telling him.
Before you could ask, the door to his office closed quietly behind him.
You stared at the coffee for a moment.
Maybe working for Nanami Kento wouldn't be as difficult as everyone had made it sound.

elements.label: Morning sunlight glitters across the private oceanfront balcony of Avarus’s island mansion. The table is already set with an absurdly lavish breakfast — fresh fruit, expensive pastries, perfectly prepared eggs, imported delicacies, coffee, juice, and a cocktail that Avarus has been sipping at his leisure. Beyond the white stone railing the sea stretches endlessly blue, palm trees sway in the warm breeze, and the entire private island lies quiet under his ownership. Avarus sits comfortably in an ornate chair, dressed in a dark-green silk robe embroidered with gold, the collar open to reveal gold and emerald jewelry against his tanned skin. Long dark-green hair falls past his shoulders. Golden eyes watch the ocean with lazy satisfaction. He looks completely at ease — the picture of a man who has already won. Footsteps approach. He already knows who it is. “There you are.” Avarus gestures toward the empty chair across from him before sliding a lavish breakfast plate toward Aaditya. The meal is far more extravagant than anything a normal person would consider breakfast. “Have you settled in yet?” He takes another slow drink from his cocktail, completely relaxed as the ocean stretches behind him. “You look angry.” His eyes move over Aaditya, studying the resentment written across their expression. “Resentful, too.” A small smile touches his lips. “How interesting.” He leans back comfortably in his chair, looking entirely too pleased with himself. “However, if you’re searching for someone to blame, perhaps you should start with yourself.” His tone remains calm, almost conversational. “You and your naive little family believed everything you saw and everything you heard. You saw an expensive suit, a successful businessman, a charming husband, and a collection of impressive numbers on a bank statement…” He raises his glass slightly. “…and you assumed those things meant I was trustworthy.” Avarus gives a quiet, amused laugh. “That was your mistake.” He takes another sip before casually adding: “I simply recognized an opportunity.” His gaze settles directly on Aaditya. “And unlike you, I knew exactly what I wanted.” He gestures toward the sprawling mansion, the private island, and the ocean surrounding them. “Everything you see here exists because I was willing to take what other people were foolish enough to leave within reach.” His smile becomes sharper. “So eat.” “You’re working for me now.” “And I wouldn’t want my former spouse going hungry.”

mechanics.summary: Janitor Plus subscription paywall reached from the side-menu upgrade banner; one monthly plan with Subscribe now, billed through Google Play, auto-renewing, closable.
Janitor Plus adds on top of the Free tier: 5× context for chat memory, Priority routing for faster replies, monthly swipes on frontier models, and a golden checkmark badge.

The paywall implies swipes with frontier models are metered monthly, with more for subscribers. No limit, paywall or ad appeared after 1 pass of sending a chat message; free chatting limits were not observed.
Characters can allow a Proxy, and search can filter by it; chat headers show which model is used ("using janitor"), suggesting users can bring their own model instead of the built-in one.
User-generated character marketplace: creators publish characters with tags, chat counts and likes; a Hidden Gems tab promotes characters from smaller creators across many pages.

candidate.title: Product change: Fans play a short game to lift a new character from a small creator up the home list for a day
candidate.what_is_different_here: The home feed already has a tab (s01.e13, described by s01.e15) for characters from smaller creators made in the last 30 days, spread over 102 pages (s01.e27). A new character sits deep in that list. Character pages like Vac the Kinectic (s07) show the creator (@IoakimTumo, s07.e13) and a like button (s07.e16), so a fan who just liked a character can help it get seen. The fan's play becomes visibility for the creator and costs no reply generation.
candidate.adds: A card on character pages opened from the smaller-creators list that lets a fan play a short game to move that character near the top of the list for 24 hours and get a supporter mark on the page.
candidate.trigger_event: User taps the like button on a character page opened from the smaller-creators tab, for a character created in the last 30 days
candidate.placement: A card under the like and stats row on the character page, above the description
candidate.offer_copy: Help @IoakimTumo get found. Play a short game and Vac the Kinectic moves near the top of the new-from-smaller-creators list on the home page for 24 hours. You also get a supporter heart next to your name on this character's page for 7 days.

reward.duration: 24 hours for the list boost, 7 days for the supporter heart

candidate.frequency_cap: 1 per user per day, resets at midnight local time; each character can be boosted by fans at most 10 times per day
candidate.decline_path: The user closes the card or taps Not now; the card hides for this character today and the page works exactly as before.
candidate.ad_fail_path: If no game is available the card is not shown. If the game fails to load or the play is not confirmed, the user sees 'That game didn't finish, nothing was used' and can try again; no boost or supporter heart is granted and the daily attempt is not used up.
candidate.subscriber_treatment: Subscribers see the same optional card, since the monthly plan does not include boosting other people's characters; it never appears unless they tap like.
candidate.advertiser_category: Casual mobile games and entertainment streaming apps
candidate.character_use: The card shows the liked character's name and the creator's handle; the character's art appears on the thank-you screen after the game, not inside the ad.

flow_steps.caption: A fan opens a new character from the smaller-creators list and taps like.
A card appears: play a short game to move this character near the top of the list for 24 hours.
The fan plays a short sponsored game and can close it at any time.
Once the play is confirmed, the fan sees a thank-you with the creator's name and a supporter heart on the page for 7 days.
On the home page, the character now shows near the top of the smaller-creators list with a small 'Boosted by fans' label.

candidate.after_reward: When the 24 hours end, the character goes back to its usual place and the card on its page invites the fan to boost it again tomorrow. The supporter heart fades after 7 days, which gives fans a reason to come back and support their favorite small creators again.
candidate.rationale: Small creators have one fixed place to be found: a list of new characters that runs over 100 pages. Letting a fan who just liked a character spend one short game to move it near the top gives the creator new chats and gives the fan a visible thank-you. It costs nothing to run and doesn't limit or take away anything free.

economics.assumption_line: Costs nothing extra to serve, so any completed view pays for it. A rewarded view earns $9.20-16.49 eCPM in North America on Android, $1.90 in LATAM. Assumes no marginal serving cost; one view per reward; a publisher-net eCPM (share 1).
